business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Cairo, national unitary administrative registration zone)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil-law system of French derivation with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; unitary state without sub-state tax or corporate-law autonomy; company formation and investment regulated at national level.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-US Trade and Investment Framework Agreement
GAFTA (Greater Arab Free Trade Area) intra-Arab trade and investment liberalization
Egypt-UK Double Taxation Agreement and the wider Egyptian DTA network (50+ states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019, and its Executive Regulations; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended) and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, each requiring an LLC to maintain an internal beneficial-ownership register identifying any individual owning or controlling more than 25% of shares or voting rights; FRA and CBE KYC/AML circulars applicable to financial intermediaries and registered agents.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: no public UBO register exists; UBO data is filed with and accessible to GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Tax Authority and bank/AML supervisory authorities, but is not published.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of corporate shareholder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registrar of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and fixing the initial capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary/notary in the home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporation counsel/agent
Certified passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner, director and authorized signatory
Bank reference/undertaking letter issued for the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's bank in the home or operating jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the Egyptian EMLCU terrorist-financing list, UN Security Council consolidated and sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and EU consolidated sanctions list; enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification; screening results must be documented in the pre-incorporation AML file and retained for at least five years after deregistration of the entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Egypt Business Center electronic platform (www.gafi.gov.eg) - one-stop shop for name search, reservation and LLC incorporation; for companies formed under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, the Commercial Registration Office of the Ministry of Trade and Industry performs the statutory name check in parallel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in Arabic; foreign shareholders may register an Arabic transliteration of their Latin-script name as the official name, and a non-binding Latin transcription is annotated on the commercial extract; any foreign-language name used on letterheads or invoices must appear together with the Arabic corporate name; the name must be distinguishable from all existing registrations and must not violate public order, morals or religious norms.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Cairo or other governorate names implying state or municipal affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, a reconsideration request may be filed with the same GAFI committee within 15 days of the electronic rejection notice; if refused again, an administrative appeal lies to the State Council (Cairo Administrative Court) within 60 days of the written refusal; in parallel, the applicant may immediately reserve up to three alternative names in a single resubmission without additional legal steps.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as a statutory seat: Egyptian law requires a physical registered office evidenced by a registered lease or title deed. A serviced-office contract providing a dedicated physical suite, a meeting room and a records room is accepted; a pure virtual mailbox or PO Box is rejected by GAFI and the Commercial Registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 15 to 20% probability of an unannounced GAFI, Tax Authority or Companies Registry compliance inspection within the first 12 months for a re-invoicing/trading LLC; the entity must keep the registered office attended during business hours, store accounting records and UBO registers at that office, and demonstrate commercial substance through local management, board minutes, operating bank accounts and active trade correspondence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones)

Consular legalization of four foreign corporate documents (good standing, board resolution, POA, certified passport copies)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule and prevailing market authentication fees (USD 120 to 150 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation and attestation of translated foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited certified translation office in Egypt
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for licensed court-attested translators

UBO-register setup and mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN and EU sanctions screening of beneficial owners

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal counsel - pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting of MOA/AOA and shareholders' internal documents, filing and post-clearance follow-up
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee per prevailing market benchmark for standard LLC incorporation with UBO due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, Articles 83-97 (Limited Liability Companies), as amended by Law No. 94 of 2005 and Law No. 145 of 2019; Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982 (as amended); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 22-27.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop (Investor Service Center), acting jointly with the Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Taasis / Nizam Al-Shirkah) authenticated by the Notary Public Authority and submitted to the GAFI One-Stop Shop for issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a trading/re-invoicing LLC under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and current GAFI practice; the founders determine the capital in the Articles of Association. Any subscribed cash capital is deposited into a temporary bank account opened in the company's name, and a bank capital-deposit certificate is filed with GAFI; no escrowed or blocked minimum capital is mandated for this non-regulated commercial activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the quota capital of the Company, fully subscribed by the founding shareholders as detailed in the Memorandum and Articles of Association authenticated before the Notary Public, is hereby ratified and allotted to the subscribers. RESOLVED FURTHER that the premises at the registered address in the Governorate of Cairo are adopted as the registered office of the Company, and that the corporate governance charter, banking mandate, and signatory schedule for the formation period are approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the General Manager and managers are appointed, with authority to execute all filings before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority, and to open bank accounts for re-invoicing settlements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Investor Service Center) online investor portal, in coordination with the Commercial Registry name database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the formation applicant on the GAFI digital portal; submit up to five proposed Arabic/Latin company names describing the ISIC 4690 re-invoicing trade; pay the name reservation fee; obtain the official name clearance letter. Foreign shareholders must have passports legalized by the Egyptian consulate and translated into Arabic by an accredited translator.
required_dossiers: Copy of national ID or passport for each founding shareholder
Legalized passport copies for non-resident shareholders
Notarized power of attorney appointing the formation lawyer
Five proposed company names with ISIC activity statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or public-order conflict, file an administrative objection with the GAFI Legal Department or resubmit an amended name list; the first correction round does not incur an additional reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Authority (Maslahat Al-Shahr Al-Aqari Wal-Tawtheeq) and a commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association specifying quota distribution, managers, and the re-invoicing activity. Before notarization, open a temporary corporate deposit account and deposit the stated share capital to obtain a bank capital-deposit certificate. Appear before the notary with original IDs and powers of attorney for signature authentication; the notary issues the authenticated incorporation contract.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid IDs and powers of attorney of all subscribing members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rejection for defective authentication is cured by re-attestation of shareholder signatures or submission of a curative power of attorney obtained through the relevant consulate; a new notary session may be held within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Company Establishment and Commercial Registration Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Investor Service Center) and Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation contract with the GAFI One-Stop Shop; GAFI extracts the establishment certificate and registers the company in the Commercial Register, thereby completing legal personality. Pay the consolidated registration fees, obtain the commercial registration number, and request the formal 'Certificate of Establishment' for post-registration use.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney and consular attestation package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner queries the file, the applicant receives a written defect note and a 30-day cure period; resubmission of corrections is free of charge, with an appeal to the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee if rejection persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card and Electronic Invoicing Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Income Tax and Value-Added Tax departments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Visit the ETA district office with the establishment certificate to obtain the Tax Card for income tax. Register for VAT under VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 when taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold (EGP 1,000,000 for goods); apply for the e-invoicing compliance package, acquire a digital signature certificate, and link the company accounts on the ETA e-invoicing portal for re-invoicing transactions.
required_dossiers: Establishment certificate and commercial registration extract
Lease contract of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or erroneous registration attracts penalties under ETA procedures; file a correction application and request remission before the ETA penalty committee with all supporting justifications documented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Completions: Official Gazette, Social Insurance, and GOEIC Import/Export Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette (Al-Jaridah Al-Rasmiyah), National Social Insurance Authority, and General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory publication of the incorporation contract in the Official Gazette; enroll the company with the Social Insurance Authority if staff are hired; for re-invoicing trade involving cross-border goods movements, register on the GOEIC platform to obtain the import/export registration certificate and customs code for transactions under ISIC 4690.
required_dossiers: Lease contract and civil defense clearance
GOEIC registration application with activity code 4690
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in the gazette filing or GOEIC certificate are cured by resubmission after correcting stamp duty or product-list data; appeals against refusal are lodged with the GOEIC complaints committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - pure re-invoicing trading activity requires no industrial permit. If bonded warehousing or physical distribution is later introduced, the General Authority for Industrial Development (GAID) and the relevant municipal licensing office would issue a separate operating permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - the Commercial Registration Certificate and Tax Card cover the re-invoicing activity; cross-border movements additionally require the GOEIC Import/Export Registration Certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category (C) non-industrial service activity; a full EIA report is not required for registered-office re-invoicing. A screening-level rapid environmental assessment is triggered only if bonded warehousing of goods is subsequently added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or emission limits are applicable at the registered office. Any later warehouse facility must comply with Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020 and EEAA ministerial decrees on solid waste segregation, noise, and fire-water runoff control.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety (Civil Defense) Certificate from the Ministry of Interior Civil Defense Administration for the registered office and any ancillary storage area; structural safety inspection under Building Law No. 119 of 2008; occupational health clearance and labor social insurance enrollment under Social Insurance Law No. 148 of 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Cairo, Egypt. Unified national portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipts clearing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; non-resident registration desk and taxpayer service center at ETA headquarters (Mohandessin).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: (1) Incorporate at GAFI (General Authority for Investment) and complete Commercial Registry (Sijil) formalities with notarized Arabic Articles of Association; (2) obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate and open a corporate bank account with an Egyptian authorized bank; (3) file ETA registration forms through the unified portal to obtain the TIN (File Number) and electronic tax card within 30 days of commercial registration; (4) register for VAT on ETA Form No. 101 within 30 days of any month in which the value of taxable supplies exceeds EGP 500,000, or immediately if export activity is expected to exceed the threshold; (5) complete mandatory e-invoicing onboarding: issue digital signature certificate, register API credentials (OAuth2), integrate ERP with the ETA sandbox, and obtain the Fiscal Code stamp; (6) appoint a resident tax representative for procedural notifications if the LLC has no local office. The TIN is the single identity key for CIT, VAT, stamp tax, and electronic invoice clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - An Egyptian LLC is mandatorily a resident corporate taxpayer under Law No. 91/2005 (Income Tax), Law No. 82/2020 (Tax Procedures), and Law No. 67/2016 (VAT). No pass-through or check-the-box regime exists; the LLC is taxed on worldwide income at entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law provides no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; the LLC is a separate CIT and VAT taxpayer. Available statutory elections are limited to: (a) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 exemption threshold to secure input VAT refunds on export costs; (b) election of fiscal year for income tax purposes; (c) depreciation method election (straight-line or declining balance) subject to ETA approval; (d) 5-year tax loss carryforward election with ETA notification and documentation; (e) reverse-charge self-accounting for imported services is mandatory under Law 67/2016 Art. 22 for services consumed in Egypt and is not an optional election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and services in Egypt; mandatory registration applies once turnover exceeds this threshold, while small taxpayers below the threshold are exempt but may voluntarily register; non-residents carrying on taxable activities in Egypt are subject to the same aggregated threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing and e-receipts in Egypt (ETA Decision No. 550/2020 and subsequent technical rules, phased by taxpayer turnover and fully applicable to all VAT-registered taxpayers by FY 2023/2024). B2B and export invoices must be generated in the taxpayer's ERP, converted to the ETA XML/JSON schema, and submitted in real time via REST/SOAP APIs with OAuth2 authentication and digital signature certificates. The ETA 'Mossar' system validates schema, performs duplicate checks, cross-checks commercial registry and tax classification, and issues an approval with a 2D barcode 'Fiscal Code' that must appear on the final invoice. Any invoice rejected by the ETA is legally invalid for input VAT deduction and cannot support export zero-rating claims. B2C e-receipts are subject to the identical real-time clearance requirement under ETA Decision No. 371/2022. Export zero-rated invoices pass through the same electronic clearance gateway.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Law No. 67 of 2016, Art. 12 (goods) and Art. 13 (services), a 0% VAT rate applies to: (1) goods physically exported from Egypt that cross the Egyptian customs border under a valid customs export declaration (Bayan Khabari / A71); and (2) services rendered to non-residents where the services are consumed entirely outside Egypt and are not linked to taxable activities within Egypt. For a re-invoicing hub, the entity must hold the principal customs export declaration, the transport document evidencing departure from Egypt, and bank evidence of receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency. Pure offshore-to-offshore re-invoicing contracts in which goods never enter Egyptian customs territory fall outside the Egyptian VAT scope and require no ETA VAT filing, subject to corporate income tax permanent establishment analysis for the trading activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan Khabari / A71) certified by the Egyptian Customs Authority evidencing physical exit of the goods
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing Egypt as the shipment origin
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit advice from an Egyptian authorized bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Zero-rated commercial invoice, sale purchase agreement, and Incoterms statement
ETA e-invoice approved with Fiscal Code, together with cargo manifest and certificate of origin where re-exported goods are involved
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to ETA desk audits and field inspections under a 5-year assessment statute of limitations (6 years for fraud). Missing or contradictory customs, transport, or FX documentation triggers automatic recharacterization as a domestic taxable supply and assessment at 14% VAT plus a late-payment surcharge of 2% per month on the tax due under Law 67/2016 Art. 73. Deliberately false export documentation constitutes tax evasion under Law 67/2016 Art. 74 and Law 82/2020 Art. 52, punishable by imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years and/or a fine of EGP 50,000 to EGP 5,000,000 or 100% of the evaded tax, whichever is greater, together with retrospective clawback of all VAT refunded and denial of the zero-rate privilege. The Central Bank of Egypt may additionally impose penalties under Law No. 194 of 2020 Art. 35 for failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Banking Supervision and Foreign Exchange Operations Department, supported by the Ministry of Finance and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for registration and capital account purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a liberalized managed-float exchange rate regime recognized under Law No. 194 of 2020 (the Central Bank and Banking System Law). Current account convertibility is generally free for trade and service transactions backed by documentary evidence. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, cross-border guarantees, and profit repatriation, are convertible subject to CBE registration, an authorized-dealer bank, and the absence of administrative suspension or sanction-flagging. Profit remittance by a re-invoicing LLC requires an outbound attestation from the tax authority (recent tax clearance), audited accounting evidence, and confirmation that the commercial invoice and customs documentation are internally consistent. Non-resident shareholders may repatriate dividends and capital gains, but the CBE may apply liquidity or documentation-based review when the bank's net open position or FX availability is constrained. Re-invoicing hubs must maintain complete trade-file documentation to avoid classification as an artificial arrangement lacking economic substance, which would trigger CBE anti-money-laundering and tax-base-erosion review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE regulations, export proceeds from goods and services must be received in Egypt through an authorized bank within 90 days from the date of shipment for goods (extendable, with justification, to 4 months for certain bulk or deferred payment goods). There is no mandatory percentage conversion into Egyptian pounds under the managed-float regime; proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account at an authorized bank, sold on the interbank market, or used for eligible trade settlements. The re-invoicing LLC must ensure that each export shipment is covered by a single Electronic Import/Export Registration on the CBE/NAFEIZA trade platform, that the proceeds are remitted via SWIFT/telex in accordance with the shipment's export declaration, and that the receiving bank obtains a cumulative confirmation of proceeds for filing. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline exposes the entity to penalties, denial of banking services, and CBE blacklisting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with limited FX desk
Operational Account with multi-currency and e-banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Egypt does not recognize foreign electronic-money institution (EMI) licenses as standing alone; a foreign EMI cannot open a CBE-supervised settlement account or conduct payment services without obtaining a CBE license or partnering with a licensed Egyptian bank / payment service provider under the CBE's FinTech regulatory sandbox (RegLab). An offshore EMI may provide ancillary treasury aggregation or reporting software, but actual clearing, settlement, foreign exchange, and Documentary Credit issuance must pass through a CBE-authorized bank. Using an unlicensed offshore EMI for EGP flows or trade payments carries significant AML, sanctions, and banking-license risk and would be rejected during corporate KYC profiling.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned LLC conducting re-invoicing trade, at least one director, the ultimate beneficial owner, or an authorized signatory holding a notarized, apostilled/consular-legalized Power of Attorney must appear physically at the bank's branch to complete signing, biometric verification, and the compliance interview. Fully remote account opening is generally unavailable for new foreign-owned structures; CBE-approved e-KYC may support preliminary screening, but account activation requires a physical signature verification session (in-branch or with a bank-notarized courier standard) and confirmation of the customer's business model. Non-resident UBOs must be identified via valid passports, source-of-wealth statements, and bank references, with all corporate documents legalized/a postilled to satisfy the 2002 AML Law and CBE CRM regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO structure opaqueness or undisclosed intermediate holding chain in a high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration form, corporate registry extract for each layer of the ownership chain, certified passport copies of all direct and indirect shareholders, bank reference letter from the applicant's relationship bank, and a chain-of-title chart covering the 25% and above threshold ownership interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Re-invoicing trade mismatch: invoice values or counterparties inconsistent with bills of lading, customs entries, or payment instructions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master international sale/purchase agreement, intercompany pricing policy with OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation (where related-party transactions exist), detailed commercial invoices showing INCOTERMS 2020, bills of lading/airway bills, customs export/import declarations, packing lists, inspection certificates, and a documented trade flow narrative demonstrating goods movement and payment mirroring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions list, adverse media, or negative regulatory hits on any principal, customer, or counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions and PEP screening output from a recognized compliance database, negative-news search results for the UBO and directors, sworn declarations from each principal, remediation memo prepared by the compliance officer, and documentary evidence that any match is a false positive (name variation, country list, or date of birth distinction).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds for capital injection, shareholder loans, or initial working capital cannot be independently verified
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of investor bank statements, audited financial statements of the investor entity, duly executed share subscription agreement and loan facility agreement, evidence of lawful origin of funds (dividends, tax filings, contract settlements), tax clearance certificate for the remitting entity, and the CBE-approved capital entry declaration demonstrating the FX routing path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status of the UBO, director, or authorized signatory combined with the high-volume re-invoicing model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration on a recognized questionnaire, comprehensive source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report, enhanced due diligence package including independent counsel opinion, senior-management approval memo from the bank, and a list of the PEP's commercial holdings to distinguish legitimate trade volume from a concealment risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing requires the shareholder or lender to remit foreign currency through a CBE-authorized bank in Egypt to a designated 'Capital Escrow' or 'Frozen Account' registered in the LLC's name. The remitting instruction must carry an accurate purpose code consistent with the underlying Palestinian-Origin, Gulf, or global capital contribution (foreign direct investment equity, shareholder loan, or pre-export finance). The receiving bank will require the LLC's board resolution approving the injection, the share subscription or facility agreement, a certified copy of the commercial registration and GAFI/Investment certification, and a UBO/source-of-funds declaration. The bank then performs a currency conversion at the interbank market rate (or credits the foreign-currency account) and, upon verified receipt, releases the funds into the operational account in accordance with the CBE's capital account regime. For loans, the facility must be registered with the CBE to secure future debt-service outbound transfers and to avoid loan-equity reclassification under thin capitalization rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements are executed through authorized banks using SWIFT MT103 (customer payment) with MT202 cover for interbank clearing, conventional Telegraphic Transfer instructions, and, for documentary trade, Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance L/Cs), standby L/Cs, or documentary collections (D/P and D/A). The re-invoicing LLC's payment instruction must be fully backed by the trade file: purchase order, final confirmed invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, customs entries, inspection report, and any CBE import/export registration reference. The bank will verify the underlying transaction, confirm the availability of foreign currency, and, where required, apply the CBE's margin or anti-avoidance checks for related-party payments. The LLC should use bank-integrated trade finance and host-to-host e-banking channels to capture full audit trails and ensure settlements clear on a same-day or next-day basis under Egyptian liquidity conditions. For multi-currency disbursements, the LLC must manage EGP/Central secondary currency pair conversions under the CBE's permitted conversion calendar and maintain sufficient cleared balances in the settlement currency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (DF) contract against verified documentary trade exposure
Cross-currency swap (CCS) between USD, EUR, GBP, and EGP with a CBE-authorized bank

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) executed through an offshore affiliate of an Egyptian authorized dealer, permitted only for hedging defineable net open trade exposure and subject to CBE position and purpose limitations
FX option sleeves embedded in approved trade financing facilities when offered by the authorized bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April for a 31 December year-end, i.e., within 4 months after the close of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay interest on unpaid tax plus late-filing fines up to EGP 50,000; additional assessment up to 30% for inaccurate or incomplete returns; administrative attachment of bank accounts and administrative strike-off for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Transfer Pricing Disclosure Return (Form No. 21)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Transfer Pricing Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the annual Corporate Income Tax Return (30 April for a December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EGP 50,000-200,000 for non-filing under the transfer pricing regime; re-pricing audit adjustments on non-arm's-length transactions plus monthly delay interest on the additional tax assessed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Certified Shareholder List (GAFI filing after General Assembly approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General Assembly approval within 3 months of fiscal year-end; GAFI filing within 15 days after approval and in all cases by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Companies Law 159/1981 up to EGP 20,000; suspension of GAFI clearance certificates blocking corporate amendments and import/export permits; judicial strike-off of the entity for repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GAFI Commercial Registry Renewal and Annual Fee Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during January following the calendar year or within 30 days of issuance of the GAFI annual renewal voucher
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrearage surcharge of 10% per annum on the unpaid fee; administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry after 60 days' public notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Final Settlement and Reconciliation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the close of the fiscal year (31 January for a 31 December year-end), in addition to monthly VAT returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay interest on VAT differences; additional tax up to 40% on under-declared output VAT; suspension of the tax card and criminal liability for tax evasion

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory annual statutory audit for all Egyptian LLCs irrespective of size, revenue, or assets; no de minimis or revenue-based exemption exists under Companies Law 159/1981 and Investment Law 72/2017
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), converged with IFRS; audit performed by a CPA registered on the ETA auditors' roll and the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors; books and tax records legally retained for a minimum of 5 years under Tax Law 91/2005, with 7 years adopted as the entity's compliance standard

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO return is currently operational in Egypt; AML Law 80/2002 (as amended) requires continuous UBO identification and record-keeping, while the GAFI annual filing package containing a certified and notarized current shareholder list serves as the de facto annual ownership confirmation; any LLC share transfer must be executed by notarized deed and filed with GAFI within 30 days
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (General Assembly and Management Resolutions)
Share Transfer Ledger containing Notarized Transfer Deeds

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400-1,200 per annum for registered office and GAFI-accredited compliance agent in Cairo or Giza
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500-3,500 per annum for a medium-risk cross-border re-invoicing entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on net taxable corporate profit (Law No. 91 of 2005, Art. 8 as amended by Law No. 96 of 2015)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Commercial free-zone treatment possible (annual gross-revenue fee of 1% to 3% in lieu of CIT); SCZone and SEZ projects may obtain a 5-year CIT holiday; small taxpayers with annual turnover up to EGP 20 million may elect simplified presumptive rates of 0.5% (up to EGP 500K), 1.5% (EGP 500K-3M), 2.5% (EGP 3M-10M) and 6% (EGP 10M-20M); no general patent-box or super-deduction is available for trading intermediaries

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return); mandatory e-filing on the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) portal at https://www.incometax.gov.eg using the unified e-tax account; audited financial statements, tax reconciliation, and transfer pricing disclosure must be attached as PDF files
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and full settlement within four months after the end of the fiscal year (a December year-end LLC must file by 30 April of the following year); the ETA may grant a 30-day extension upon written request and payment of estimated remaining tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced sales proceeds of the re-invoicing hub, including goods resold to Egyptian or MENA customers; purchase-sale intermediation must be reported here when title passes through the Egyptian LLC
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders with an Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) booked through the LLC must report the PE-attributable Egyptian-source turnover; pure offshore trading without Egyptian activities is not reportable by a non-resident unless a PE exists

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods purchased for on-sale; for re-invoicing structures only the cost associated with goods resold and shipped under the Egyptian LLC's contracts is deductible; related-party purchase prices must be arm's length
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should not claim a deduction unless the expense is incurred through the Egyptian PE and supported by invoices, customs declarations, and banking evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 1 minus Line 2; for general re-invoicing trade the margin must correspond to documented economic functions, assets, and risks of the Egyptian intermediary (normally a 2% to 5% resale-margin or TNMM net margin)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE's gross profit must be computed separately for Egyptian operations; intercompany cost allocations require time records and a head-office expense schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Freight management, warehousing, bank charges, salaries, rent, professional fees, and marketing costs allocable to the re-invoicing trade; all deductions require valid invoices, bank settlement, and registration in the ETA e-invoice system
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically incurred in Egypt for the PE are deductible; head-office general management costs are deductible only within ETA cost-allocation guidelines

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per statutory books before tax adjustments; must equal audited financial statement profit subject to the tax reconciliation table
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must compute taxable profit using the separate-entity fiction under Article 33 of Law 91/2005; an unjustified re-invoicing margin below 1% invites a transfer pricing adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of entertainment expenses (only 50% deductible), penalties and fines, interest on shareholder loans exceeding the thin-capitalization safe harbor, unrealized exchange differences, and related-party markups not supported by transfer pricing documentation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident lenders may be disallowed when the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds the safe harbor; documentation must establish commercial rationale for the Egyptian intermediary

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct the annual utilization of prior-year tax losses (maximum 5-year carryforward period, no carryback); losses from the re-invoicing trade may be used against Egyptian-source income and remain subject to ownership continuity rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unutilized PE losses may not offset non-resident income outside Egypt and are forfeited when the PE is deregistered

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 - Tax Due on Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Multiply taxable income by the 22.5% headline rate or the SME presumptive rate where the LLC validly elected the simplified regime; foreign tax credits for withholding suffered on export income are claimed in this section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same rate applies to PE-attributable profit; the LLC's profit is not taxed at the shareholder level until distribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct quarterly provisional instalments already paid, any final withholding tax levied on Egyptian-source income, and eligible foreign tax credits under Law 91/2005 or the applicable DTA
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot credit Egyptian dividend WHT against the LLC's CIT; only taxes directly borne by the PE are creditable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - Net Tax Payable / Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final settlement figure; overpayment is refundable by the ETA or carried forward with interest only after a tax audit; underpayment attracts monthly delay tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Repatriation of profits must be executed through the Egyptian banking system and cannot be processed before the final tax settlement certificate is issued

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and non-payment: delay tax accrues at 2% per month (or fraction of a month) on the unpaid amount; administrative fines of EGP 1,000 to EGP 20,000 per unfiled or defective return; submission of false declarations triggers Article 133 criminal prosecution

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Transfer Pricing Related-Party Disclosure Form (annexed to Form No. 19) with optional Country-by-Country Report notification; submitted through the same ETA e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing simultaneously with Form No. 19 (within four months after fiscal year-end); CbCR notification must be filed with the ETA e-CbCR module before the last day of the reporting fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Listing of all controlled transactions in the fiscal year: sales of goods, purchases, services, financing, royalties, and management fees; categorize by counterparty and disclose the Egyptian margin
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and affiliates must be identified with TINs; transactions with UAE or offshore flow-through entities must be disclosed and mapped to an economic substance indicator

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the most appropriate method: resale price method for the re-invoicing hub's goods resale; TNMM net margin as a secondary benchmark; intercompany agreements and benchmark studies must be attached
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Selection must be consistent with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; a one-page contemporaneous benchmark summary is required at filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm the absence or ownership of commercial intangibles, describe contractual risk-taking (currency, credit, and inventory risk), and identify capital deployment of the Egyptian entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A limited-risk distributor profile must be documented; evidence that the UAE parent retains risks while the LLC books only the margin may lead to recharacterization

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to submit complete documentation: administrative fine up to EGP 20,000 and delay tax of 2% per month on the transfer pricing adjustment; the ETA may disregard the taxpayer's audit position and impose a full correction on the margin

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding tax under Articles 56-57 of Law 91/2005, charged on cash and in-kind distributions of the LLC; the LLC must withhold at distribution and remit the tax to the ETA within the statutory WHT return deadline
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a DTA-reduced dividend rate (commonly 5% or 10%), the non-resident beneficiary must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) certified by its home-country tax authority for the relevant calendar year; obtain an Egyptian TIN in the shareholder's name and appoint an Egyptian tax representative; file the ETA treaty-relief application form with the International Transactions Unit before the dividend payment date, attaching the TRC, board resolution, ownership certificates, and UBO declaration; after receiving the ETA authorization the reduced rate applies; where no authorization is obtained, the 10% WHT remains final and may be recovered through the Article 57 refund route within the five-year statute of limitations
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 20% on royalties for industrial, commercial, or technical intellectual property (Article 59); 20% on loan interest paid to non-resident lenders (Article 58), with a carve-out for foreign bank loans financing Egyptian projects at commercial rates; most Egyptian DTAs (including Egypt-UAE and Egypt-UK) limit dividend WHT to 5%-10%, interest to 10%-15%, and royalties to 10%-15%, subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership satisfaction

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8 million of related-party transactions in any single annual transaction category (goods, services, financing, intangibles) triggers mandatory Master File and Local File preparation; multinational groups with consolidated group revenue at or above EGP 50 billion must additionally file Country-by-Country Report with the ETA
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but the ETA enforces the Article 36 arm's length principle, general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR), and place-of-effective-management (POEM) analysis under Article 31 of Law 91/2005 to disregard or recharacterize transactions lacking commercial rationality; a re-invoicing LLC must evidence its own employees, premises, board control, trade documentation, and bank accounts in Egypt; otherwise tainted dividends, deemed PE income, denied treaty benefits, and reassessment may follow

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False or Suppressed Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of the re-invoicing margin, suppression of invoices, double invoicing, or submission of falsified customs and shipping documents to the ETA to conceal taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 133 of Law 91/2005: imprisonment for three to five years and a fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000, plus recovery of the evaded tax and delay tax of 2% per month; confiscation of documents and equipment used in the evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who signed false returns face joint and several liability for the unpaid CIT, uncollected WHT, and penalty surcharges; the ETA may issue a travel ban and refer the directors to criminal court; conviction results in disqualification from board positions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing goods at a sub-margin below 1%, creating circular purchase and resale flows with UAE affiliates, failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File and Master File despite exceeding the EGP 8 million threshold, and relying on unverified comparables in the benchmark study
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA recharacterization of the full profit, disallowance of the related-party markup, delay tax of 2% per month on the adjusted tax, administrative penalty up to EGP 20,000, and a 5-year reassessment window extended to 6 years for willful concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the adjusted tax difference where they directed the transfer pricing policy knowingly; an egregious margin may be reclassified as a disguised dividend, producing a 10% WHT assessment against the LLC and personal recovery against the approving manager

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Egyptian LLC operates without employees, office, trade contracts, or bank accounts; functions purely as an invoicing pass-through; or holds board meetings exclusively outside Egypt while the non-resident parent makes all substantial decisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the GAAR and POEM rules re-attributing profits: the ETA may tax the entire re-invoicing margin at 22.5%, deny treaty benefits, impose 10% deemed-dividend WHT, and request the Commercial Registry to dissolve the company for false status declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing under Articles 49 and 73 of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981: directors, auditors, and signatory managers are jointly liable for company obligations when the company is used as a facade; travel restrictions and asset seizures may be ordered to secure tax claims

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Violations on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends or deemed profit distributions to non-resident shareholders without deducting 10% dividend WHT, paying interest or royalties abroad without 20% WHT, or claiming treaty-reduced rates without a valid TRC and ETA authorization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The LLC remains liable for the full withholding amount plus delay tax of 2% per month from the due date, an additional recovery fine of 20% of the uncollected amount, and criminal prosecution of the legal representative where the failure was deliberate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general manager and board signatories are joint and several debtors for the uncollected WHT; the ETA may issue charge orders on the LLC's bank accounts after 30 days of formal summons; imprisonment applies in cases of systematic distributions to shell shareholders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Re-invoicing trade structured to move funds through third-party countries or free zones with no underlying goods movement, accepting untraceable cash or crypto settlement, structuring wire transfers below reporting thresholds, or failing to file suspicious-transaction reports with the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (EMLCU)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 14 and 17 of AML Law No. 80 of 2002: imprisonment of three to seven years and a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000, forfeiture of the instrumentalities and proceeds, and freezing of bank accounts; the EMLCU may suspend the trade license upon referral to the Public Prosecutor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face imprisonment and personal fines if they knowingly execute or authorize suspicious trade transactions; the court may impose a travel ban during the criminal investigation and order disqualification from any financial or commercial management functions in Egypt
